Hi Jordan,

Thanks for downloading our "LLM Inference Benchmark Report" — hope you found the charts on latency vs cost for common seq lengths helpful. I saw your download come through and wanted to check whether you'd be open to a short demo so we can walk through the results and show how Redwood might map to your workload.

If helpful, we can cover:
- how the benchmark maps to 1-10ms token latency targets,
- batching/kv-cache strategies to reduce token cost, and
- model/quantization recommendations for similar analytics workloads.

Are you free for a 30-min slot in the next few days? I'm available:
- Thu 6/17 9:00–11:00 AM PT
- Thu 6/17 3:00–5:00 PM PT
- Fri 6/18 8:30–11:30 AM PT

Or feel free to grab a time on my calendar: https://calendly.com/redwood-marissa/30min

I'll also attach a short highlights PDF summarizing the benchmark takeaways in case you want to skim first.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0173

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference with predictable latency and cost

Attachment: benchmark-highlights.pdf

From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmeanalytics.com>

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the follow-up and the highlights PDF.

We're the analytics infra team at Acme Analytics (I'm Jordan, VP of Platform). A few quick context notes:
- We run mixed workloads (batch scoring + some low-latency inference for dashboards), typical seq lengths 256–1024 tokens.
- Current infra is a mix of managed GPUs and CPU-based embeddings; we're evaluating tradeoffs to reduce per-token cost while keeping dashboard latencies under 200ms.

A quick demo sounds great. Any chance you have availability Thu 6/17 at 3:30 PM PT? If that works, I'll invite a PM and one of our infra engineers.

Also: any materials you recommend we share internally before the demo (SLA, security/compliance checklist)?

—Jordan
Jordan Miller
VP, Platform — Acme Analytics

See you Thu.
